successors.note: "After the departure of the British from India in 1947, the Maharawal signed an Instrument of Accession"; Girdhar Singh (1949-1950) "was instrumental in merging his former state with" what the page calls Greater Rajasthan "in 1950". The infobox gives the end as 1947.

capitals.name: Jaisalmer
capitals.note: "In 1156 CE, Rawal Jaisal moved his capital from Lodhruva to Jaisalmer"; infobox Capitals: Lodhruva (before 1156), Jaisalmer (from 1156).

rulers.name: Rawal Jait Singh I
rulers.note: Faced a long siege by Alauddin Khalji "around 1299" (Jaisalmer State and Fort pages).

rulers.name: Rawal Lunkaran Singh
rulers.note: Fought Humayun in 1541 (Jaisalmer State and Fort pages).

rulers.name: Maharawal Mulraj Singh II
rulers.note: "The fort remained under the control of Mughals until 1762, when Maharawal Mulraj took control of the fort"; treaty with the East India Company on 12 December 1818; "After the death of Mulraj in 1820, his grandson Gaj Singh inherited control of the fort".

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives 41,600 km2 for 1931 and nothing for any earlier date; a 115 km circle about Jaisalmer (about 41,200 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years, so the growth of the Bhati state from the country about Lodhruva and Jaisalmer (1156) to its 20th-century extent is not drawn. The Bhati page has Rohri, Sukkur and Pugal under Bhati control "By the 12th-century" and Rao Kelana of Pugal expanding in the 15th, but names no boundary and does not tie them to Jaisalmer.

region.text: the country about Jaisalmer and the older seat Lodhruva

ledger.note: 1156: Rawal Jaisal moves the Bhati capital from Lodhruva to Jaisalmer. "In 1156 CE, Rawal Jaisal moved his capital from Lodhruva to Jaisalmer" (infobox Established 1156); the Fort page says the fort was "built in 1156 AD by the Rawal Jaisal" and calls the date a legend, and gives no date for the move itself. The Bhati page gives "Founded: 3rd century" for the kingdom and is silent on 1156. The founding land is a reading about Jaisalmer.

1949: the Maharawal's state is merged into Rajasthan. Infobox "Ended: 1947" and the text "After the departure of the British from India in 1947, the Maharawal signed an Instrument of Accession"; Jawahir Singh is listed as "last ruler of the state" to 1949 and Girdhar Singh (1949-1950) "was instrumental in merging his former state" into what the page calls Greater Rajasthan "in 1950". The year 1949 is the end of the last ruler's reign; the page does not date the merger.

wars.name: Siege of Jaisalmer by Alauddin Khalji
wars.outcome: "Around 1299 CE, Rawal Jait Singh I faced a long siege by Alauddin Khalji"; the fort stayed under Delhi Sultanate control "for a few years" afterwards (undated) before surviving Bhatis reoccupied it.
wars.note: Fort page; the date "seems to have begun in AD 1299".

wars.name: Humayun against Jaisalmer
wars.outcome: "In 1541 CE, Rawal Lunakaran also fought Mughal emperor Humayun when the latter attacked the fort on his way to Ajmer."
wars.note: The Fort page also says "Mughals controlled the fort until 1762, when Maharawal Mulraj took control of the fort", with no date for the start of that control and no mention on the Jaisalmer State page.

certainty.note: The page gives an area for 1931 and no boundary; the shape is a circle of that area for all years.

sources.title: Jaisalmer State
sources.note: Established 1156; capital moved from Lodhruva to Jaisalmer in 1156; 1541 Humayun; 1818 British protectorate; area 41,600 km2 (1931); rulers 1153-1949; accession 1947; merged into Rajasthan.

sources.title: Jaisalmer Fort
sources.note: Fort built in 1156; siege by Alauddin Khalji from 1299; Lunakaran against Humayun in 1541; "Mughals controlled the fort until 1762, when Maharawal Mulraj took control"; treaty of 12 December 1818; Mulraj died 1820.

sources.title: Bhati
sources.note: The Bhati clan: Rohri, Sukkur and Pugal under Bhati control by the 12th century; Timur sacks Bhatner 1398; Rao Kelana of Pugal in the 15th century; silent on Jaisalmer in 1156 and on Jaisalmer's extent.

notes: Three pages opened (Jaisalmer State, Jaisalmer Fort, Bhati). The pages give no boundary and no area before 1931; the late state is drawn throughout and the early extent is not known. Conflicts: end 1947 (infobox) against Jawahir Singh to 1949 and the merger "in 1950"; the British treaty on 11 December 1818 against 12 December 1818 (Jaisalmer State text against the Fort page: "The treaty between the East India Company and Mulraj on 12 December 1818"); Mughal control of the fort "until 1762" (Fort page; Jaisalmer State page says nothing of the Mughals after Humayun, 1541). Not recorded as ledger events because the pages give no land: the 1762 recovery of the fort, the 1299 occupation by the Delhi Sultanate, and the 1398 sack of Bhatner (Bhati page, which names a different Bhati ruler). british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start for jaisalmer-state from the treaty of December 1818 to 1947 ("On 11 December 1818 Jaisalmer became a British protectorate"). Counterparts: delhi-sultanate and mughal-empire (existing polities); no dossier needed from other groups.
